questions.title: What is a crafted block worth?
questions.context: We want every block to be sellable. A crafted block (like an iron block) must never pay more than the stuff it is made of, or players would craft and sell to print money.

options.label: Exactly what its parts are worth
options.detail: An iron block sells for 9 ingots' worth, never more or less. Simplest to explain, nothing to exploit.

options.label: 90% of its parts
options.detail: Crafting loses 10%, so selling raw is always a little better. Adds a tiny money sink.

options.label: One low flat price
options.detail: Every crafted block sells for about $1. Easy list, but a valuable block pays almost nothing.

questions.title: What do dirt and logs pay?
questions.context: Dirt, sand, gravel, stone and logs are free and endless on an island. If they pay real money, digging dirt becomes the best job. Wooden blocks also need a log price to be sellable at all.

options.label: Pennies: $0.25 each
options.detail: A stack of 64 pays $16. Selling clears your inventory but is not an income. Real money stays in the Depths, farms and mobs.

options.label: $1 each, like cobblestone
options.detail: A stack pays $64. Simple, but the shop must then raise dirt, sand and gravel from $4 to above $7.50 each.

options.label: Keep them unsellable
options.detail: No change from today. Goes against your wish that every block can be sold.

questions.title: How loud is the daily Hot Item?
questions.context: One item each day pays 25% more. Today players only see it if they open the sell chest. Making it visible gives people a reason to change what they mine or farm.

options.label: Chat line, join line, HOT tag
options.detail: One chat line at midnight (Oslo), one line the first time you join each day, and a HOT tag in the sell chest.

options.label: Only in the sell chest
options.detail: No chat at all. Quiet, but most players will never notice it.

options.label: Also a hologram at the sell NPC
options.detail: Everything in option a, plus a floating sign at the sell NPC in Market Square.

questions.title: A Market tips button in the sell chest?
questions.context: The sell chest could show the 5 items that pay the most above normal right now, plus the Hot Item. It helps players pick a different job each day instead of one single meta.

options.label: Yes, add it
options.detail: One extra button with a short list. Small new feature, reads data we already have.

options.label: No, keep it simple
options.detail: Players rely on the Rising and Falling words next to each price.

questions.title: Sell rare items for shards or crystals?
questions.context: Crystals can never be traded. If an item that players can trade sold for crystals, it would be a back door around that rule. Shards are tradeable and come from bosses and events.

options.label: No, selling always pays money
options.detail: Rare items drop crystals or shards directly when found. Closes the back door and keeps one simple rule.

options.label: A few rare items sell for shards
options.detail: Shards would then have a second source next to bosses and events.

options.label: A few rare items sell for crystals
options.detail: Opens a way to turn tradeable items into crystals. Not recommended.

questions.title: How much should /shop sell?
questions.context: The shop has about 253 items. Builders want choice, but blocks that come from a place or a boss are also what players trade with each other.

options.label: All ordinary blocks, 250 to 330 items
options.detail: Common building, wood, stone, color and plain decoration blocks. Nether, End, ocean and Depths blocks stay play-only so players trade them.

options.label: Keep exactly today's 253
options.detail: No growth until the shop overhaul. Safest, but builders will ask for more.

options.label: Every block that exists in survival
options.detail: About 450 or more items. Builders are happy, but the auction house loses most block trading.

questions.title: Do shop prices ever move?
questions.context: Sell prices move with demand. Shop prices are fixed numbers today, which keeps the money balance easy to control.

options.label: No, fixed prices for now
options.detail: Daily deals and a progress-locked Island tab wait for the full price overhaul.

options.label: Daily deals now
options.detail: 6 items at -20% each day, new at midnight (Oslo), same for everyone. Gives a reason to check the shop, takes a little off the money sink.

options.label: Prices rise when many buy
options.detail: Mirrors the sell side. More complex and harder to balance.

questions.title: Fixed price only, or real bidding?
questions.context: Today every listing has one fixed price. Some players like bidding on rare items, but it adds waiting and a new system.

options.label: Fixed price only
options.detail: Simple and instant. The name stays Auction house.

options.label: Fixed price plus optional bidding over $1M
options.detail: Money is held while you lead, and late bids extend the timer. Exciting for rare items, but new rules and waiting.

questions.title: One place for waiting items?
questions.context: Unsold, cancelled and returned auction items wait in a separate collection bin. /box already holds everything else that did not fit.

options.label: Yes, use /box
options.detail: Unsold and returned items go to /box tagged From auction. The collection bin goes away. One place to look.

options.label: Keep the bin, add Take all
options.detail: Two places, but each stays simple and the AH keeps its own menu.

options.label: Keep it exactly as built
options.detail: No work, but players must remember two places.

questions.title: How fast can you list items?
questions.context: Today you wait 10 seconds between listings and can list the same item type only 3 times in 30 minutes. You said no waiting unless it stops real abuse.

options.label: 2 seconds, 6 of the same item per 30 min
options.detail: Still stops scripts. The 5 listing slots stay the real limit.

options.label: Keep 10 seconds and 3 per 30 min
options.detail: As decided in answer 554. Safest against spam, slowest for traders.

options.label: No pacing, only the 5 slots
options.detail: Fastest. A script could spam the menu for a moment.

questions.title: How long can a listing run?
questions.context: Listings last 12, 24 or 48 hours. A rare, expensive item may need longer, and each relist costs the 1% fee again.

options.label: Add 7 days, same 1% fee
options.detail: Options become 12h, 24h, 48h and 7d. Fewer relists and less busywork.

options.label: Keep 12h, 24h, 48h
options.detail: As decided in the first design. Players relist rare items every two days.

options.label: Add 7 days at a 2% fee
options.detail: Longer listings cost more, so the auction stays tidy. A little more to explain.
